verdict.reasoning:
Reproduced on claude/canon-5-shimmer at f6d20c3. The build is clean and the generated files match. Six of the header picture's eleven crest 'tip' glows have their centres on the grey backdrop above or beside the crest, not on the orange feather tips. These are ART_GLOW.dino (src/app.html line 523) entries 1 to 6: (0.319, 0.029), (0.354, 0.007), (0.396, 0.002), (0.435, 0.018), (0.470, 0.029) and (0.509, 0.075). Canon says 'his eyes, feather tips and mouth-glow shimmer'. README decision 21 says the glow sits on 'eleven of the crest's orange feather tips', README test 10 says the check fails when glows move off the features, and the app.html comment says the same. So the page and its labelling disagree.

Cause: features.py's background test is 's < 0.12'. JPEG noise beside the crest has saturation 0.12 to 0.13, so the test fails there. On row 16 of the file the feather ends at x 194, and pixels 195 to 207 are grey, e.g. (203, 16) = (134, 125, 116), s 0.13. The top-edge minima (138, 16), (203, 16) and (220, 42) therefore landed on the backdrop.

On the page, the drawn glow brightens the backdrop pixel at tip 5's centre from (132, 124, 117) to (236, 218, 181) at full, +94. The backdrop at (0.47, 0.03) goes up +101 at full and +50 at the 'faint glow' strength of 0.262. A side-by-side render shows a row of pale dots floating in the grey above the crest at faint, and a ring of bright dots off the feathers at full.

pr5 [glow-features] cannot catch this. FEAT.hero copies the same six off-feature coordinates, so it measures the glow where it is drawn ('tips mean +70.6', 11 of 11). Its header controls are in the corners, the tank top and the shirt, far from the crest. So the README's claim that 'glows moved off them fail' does not hold for these six. This is a real defect: a contradiction between the labelling and what is drawn, plus a test that does not test what it says. It is not a recorded decision. It is minor because it is decoration only (aria-hidden; the tile carries the figures).

The reviewer's move of the six points is right. All six new centres fall on tan file pixels, e.g. (205, 30) = (221, 175, 113). With the full-size glow (grow 1.2), the share over the backdrop drops from 40-95% to 10-18%, and the share over tan rises from 1-31% to 55-73%. That matches tips 7 to 11, which sit 2-17% over the backdrop and 38-63% over tan.

The reviewer's proposed test control does not work, though. A control at (0.47, 0.03) with the test's usual window (half-width 3% of the width) still reads +7.3 at 1280 px and +15.4 at 390 px after the fix. That is because the window reaches the moved glows and the lit tan tips, so the fixed page fails the check's limit of 4. With a narrow window it still reads +6.2 at 390 px. A control at (0.48, 0.02) with a narrow window (0.006 of the width) works. It reads +8.3 at 1280 px and +39.0 at 390 px on the current code, so the check fails, and 0.0 at both widths after the fix, so it passes. With that control, the whole --pr5 block exits 0 on the fixed copy. After the fix the header's measured tip means change from +71 to +56 at 1280 px and from +52 to +48 at 390 px, so README test 10's figures need updating.

verdict.reasoning: I reproduced it in the engine and on the page. The lab's stomp rule counts that energy as `footing` wherever real ground would break. The page's own shimmer card states the same rule in general terms: "what would have broken the ground (Unbreakable footing: ...)". Decision 9 adds the Wrestle throw's crater-sized landing under the same rule. The arm-wrestling pin is the same case. armWrestle builds its real-ground crater from r.pin.E under the condition `pins && !holdsGround(cA) && v >= 2000 && !relativistic && isFinite(E)`, and with the power on it sets that crater to 0. takenBack still files 'arm' under TB_NONE, so it counts nothing. The engine comment and decision 22 say Arm takes back only "momentum without motion", and that is false for this run: it holds a 2.01 GJ slam out of the ground. Decision 22 states the exclusion as a fact and gives no reason, so this is not a justified recorded decision. The direct comparison: a 10^9 kg stomp with an 18.2 m real crater counts 1.14 GJ ("about a faint glow"), while a 10^9-vs-10^8 kg pin with a 19.7 m real crater counts 0 and shows no tile. findings.title: Fast game-of-catch legs show a false 'air's drag' part beside a catch that is taken back: relativistic kinetic energy in the real-air figure, Newtonian in Ecatch, plus a rounding residue past 1% of c
findings.location: rex-strength-lab/src/engine.js: takenBack's catch leg (arrive = Ecatch), tbDrag, and realAirLeg's lost() (E0 = keFromV(v0) + PE). Ecatch comes from catchIt's Newtonian 0.5 m v^2.
findings.evidence: Page (game of catch, effort All-out via #duo-effort, default powers), with the tiles as the page reads them. A fastball 10 m apart at 10^14 kg: 'Rex takes in 3.63 TJ, from the air's drag on what he threw (0.00049 J) and his catch (3.63 TJ)'. A fastball 1 km apart at 10^13 kg: '...the air's drag on what he threw (15.2 MJ) and his catch (363 GJ)'. A person 31.6 km apart at 10^12 kg: '...(544 kJ) and his catch (3.27 TJ)'. Ollie's line is the same in each. Engine, for the person leg: E0 = keFromV(vE) + PE = 3,266,347,814,055 J. Ecatch = 3,266,345,795,156 J, which is 0.5 m v^2, while keFromV(vArrive) = 3,266,347,767,938 J. Real air's take E0 - Eend = 3,266,346,338,842 J, so tbDrag leaves 543,686 J. The excess is the relativistic term keFromV adds and Ecatch leaves out (about 3/4 β^2): 6e-7 at 2.69e5 m/s, and 4.2e-5 at 2.24e6 m/s (15.2 MJ / 363 GJ). Past 1% of c (L.fast) the leftover is rounding: 4.9e-4 J out of 3.63e12 J. A sweep at the defaults (baseball, car, person, bus, shot; hard and easy; 10 m to 3,160 km; 10^5 to 10^16 kg) found 209 of 2,225 legs that reach the catcher with a drag part beside the catch. No partner toss does this. Section 9i's code-1 check covers only 10^8 and 10^9 kg legs, where the term is negligible.
findings.expected: Decision 8 and the count-once rule say the drag part is only what exceeds the arrival, 'in practice nothing'. With the catch taken back, the drag part is 0. The figure the tile labels as air drag is not drag. It is the part of the catch's energy that the Newtonian Ecatch leaves out (or rounding). Under the owner's labelling standard the tile must not name it as the air's drag.
findings.fix: Compare against the arrival in the same convention, and allow for rounding. Tried in a scratch copy: in tbDrag return 0 when x - arrive <= 1e-9 * x, and in the catch branch keep add(whoC,'catch',Ecatch) but compare against max(Ecatch, keFromV(L.vArrive, m)). The drag part is then 0 in all three page cases. The 300 m fastball at 10^8 kg and the 10 km car at 10^9 kg stay 0. Ecatch itself is a powers-off result, so it is not changed. Add a 9i check at 10^12 to 10^14 kg: drag part 0 beside each catch.

verdict.reasoning: Reproduced on the page and in the engine. In a catch leg, tbDrag subtracts L.catch.Ecatch from real air's take. Ecatch is catchIt's Newtonian 0.5 m v^2 (plus stroke terms), but realAirLeg's lost() uses keFromV, the relativistic kinetic energy. Below 1% of c the gap, about (3/4)β² of the energy, shows up as a 'drag' part. Past 1% of c (L.fast) Ecatch already equals keFromV, and what remains is one unit of floating-point rounding (0.00049 J against 3.63 TJ). Either way the figure labelled "the air’s drag on what he threw" is not drag. It is catch energy that Ecatch's convention leaves out, or round-off. That contradicts decision 8 and the shimmer card's count-once rule (drag is only what exceeds the arrival, "in practice nothing"), and it breaks the owner's labelling standard. The total is barely affected (a few parts in 10^5 or less), so this is minor. The proposed fix works: with it in a scratch copy, all three page cases and both of 9i's controls give a drag part of 0, and section 9 passes 36/36. A sweep I ran also found legs where a drag part beside a catch comes from potential energy (for example a fastball 316 km apart, whose drag-free path meets the catcher 6.6 km up). Those follow the stated rule and are not this defect; the fix leaves them alone.
verdict.reproduction: Page (js/c2page.js), game of catch, All-out, default powers. cObj baseball, hard, cLogD 1, logKg 14: 'Rex takes in 3.63 TJ, from the air’s drag on what he threw (0.00049 J) and his catch (3.63 TJ)', and the same for Ollie. cLogD 3, logKg 13: '... the air’s drag on what he threw (15.2 MJ) and his catch (363 GJ)'. cObj person, cLogD 4.5, logKg 12: '... (544 kJ) and his catch (3.27 TJ)'. Control at 300 m and 1e8 kg: 'Rex takes in 3.63 MJ, from his catch'. Engine (js/c2.js): 1 km fastball at 1e13 kg: Ecatch 363,333,231,868 J against keFromV(vArrive) 363,348,395,898 J, giving drag 15,162,903 J. 10 m fastball at 1e14 kg (fast): Ecatch 3,633,483,958,981.896 against keFromV 3,633,483,958,981.898, giving drag 0.000488 J. Fix in a scratch copy (fix2): tbDrag returns 0 when x - arrive <= 1e-9 x, and the catch branch compares against max(Ecatch, keFromV(L.vArrive, m)). The drag part becomes 0 in all five cases, the catch part is unchanged, and powers.js --skip-off --tally-only passes 36/36.
verdict.better_fix: In engine.js: `const tbDrag = (x, arrive) => (!(x > 0) || arrive === Infinity ? 0 : x === Infinity ? Infinity : x - arrive <= 1e-9 * x ? 0 : x - arrive);`. In the catch leg: `} else if (reaches && C.ownRecoil && L.catch) { add(whoC, 'catch', L.catch.Ecatch); arrive = Math.max(tbJ(L.catch.Ecatch), L.vArrive > 0 ? keFromV(L.vArrive, ob.m) : 0); }`. This compares in the same relativistic convention without changing Ecatch, which is a powers-off result. Add a 9i check: a fastball 1 km apart at 1e13 kg, a person 31.6 km apart at 1e12 kg and a fastball 10 m apart at 1e14 kg, with each catch taken back, give a drag part of exactly 0.

findings.outcome: Fixed with the skeptic's better fix: tbDrag treats a drag part of a part in 10^9 or less of real air's take as rounding (0), and a catch leg's arrival is max(Ecatch, keFromV(vArrive)), the relativistic kinetic energy of its motion as it arrives, the convention realAirLeg counts in; Ecatch itself (a powers-off result) is unchanged, and so is the catch part. Moved: a fastball 10 m apart at 10^14 kg, a drag part of 0.00049 J beside each 3.63 TJ catch, now 0; a fastball 1 km apart at 10^13 kg, 15.2 MJ beside each 363 GJ catch, now 0; a person 31.6 km apart at 10^12 kg, 544 kJ beside each 3.27 TJ catch, now 0. findings.evidence: Each mutant ran in a scratch copy with node test/powers.js --skip-off --tally-only: 36/36 pass. (a) Removing the cap: f0.air.E in place of Math.min(E1, f0.air.E). (b) tbPE(obj.m, hEnd) in place of tbPE(obj.m, f.belowStop ? 0 : hEnd). findings.fix: Add to 9i: (a) the tank at 45° at 10^16.5 kg, where the drag part equals E1 = KE(vOut) + PE(release) and never exceeds it; (b) the 10 m Ollie with a car lobbed 10 m and own recoil off, where the drag part = KE(vE) + PE(h0) - KE(vImpact at the ground) = 7,260 J, worked out in the test.

verdict.reasoning: Both mutants survive section 9, and they also survive the pull request 5 page block. I reproduced each one independently. (a) The cap binds in a run the page can reach. A tank thrown at 45° at 10^16.5 kg escapes, and its full-drag flight's air tally is 1.0031 x E1. The engine caps the figure at E1 = 2.5385e17 J; without the cap it is 2.546e17 J, more than the tank's own energy. The page shows 254 PJ on the clean build and 255 PJ on the mutant. 9c and the README claim 'never more than what was thrown' over 666 throws, but none of those throws makes the cap bind, so the check cannot catch the regression it names. (b) With Ollie 10 m tall, a car lobbed 10 m at the dial and own recoil off, the full-drag lob never reaches his 9 m hands (belowStop) and lands. The engine gives a drag part of 7,259.6 J; the mutant that drops the belowStop branch gives 0. No section 9 or page check uses a catcher taller than the thrower. One correction to the proposed check: the engine's figure is min(dragE = 7,259.6 J, E0 - Eend = 7,266.6 J), because the step sum binds. The test should therefore use its existing legReal helper, which already mirrors belowStop, not KE(vE) + PE(h0) - KE(vImpact) alone, which gives 7,266.6 J and fails against the correct engine at a 1e-9 tolerance. This is a test-coverage defect of the kind round 1 confirmed (its code-4 and code-5), so I rate it minor.
